Under the PM-KISAN scheme, the following categories of beneficiaries of higher economic status are excluded:

(a) All Institutional Land holders; and  
(b) Farmer families in which one or more of its members belong to the following categories:  
i) Former and present holders of constitutional posts  
ii) Former and present Ministers / State Ministers and former / present Members of Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha / State Legislative Assemblies / State Legislative Councils, former and present Mayors of Municipal Corporations, former and present Chairpersons of District Panchayats  
iii) All serving or retired officers and employees of Central / State Government Ministries / Offices / Departments and their field units, Central or State PSEs and Attached offices / Autonomous Institutions under Government as well as regular employees of the Local Bodies (Excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees)  
iv) All superannuated / retired pensioners whose monthly pension is Rs.10,000/- or more (Excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees)  
v) All Persons who paid Income Tax in last assessment year  
vi) Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practices  

Additionally, in case of new beneficiaries being uploaded on the PM-KISAN Portal, all land holding farmers’ families who are Non-resident Indians (NRIs) in terms of the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961 shall also be excluded from any benefit under the Scheme. Furthermore, in cases of cultivable land transferred to other persons through Sale Deed, Partition Deed, Gift Deed, etc. after 01.02.2019, the transferee will not be eligible under the Scheme.

Please note that this list of rules or conditions may be incomplete, and you should verify it on the official portal.

Under the PM-KISAN scheme, the cut-off date for the determination of eligibility of beneficiaries is 01.02.2019, and no changes after that date will be considered for eligibility for the next 5 years (except when ownership transfer takes place due to succession from death).

Sources: [pmkisan_guidelines_rev2020.pdf, page 3]

Yes, you can still get the benefits under certain conditions:

1. **Succession due to death:** If the transfer of ownership of cultivable land takes place on account of succession due to the death of the landowner (even after the cut-off date of 01.02.2019), the family of the successors is entitled to the benefits, provided they are otherwise eligible as per the scheme guidelines. 
2. **Transfer between 01.12.2018 and 31.01.2019:** If the transfer of ownership of cultivable land happened due to any reason such as purchase, succession, will, gift, etc., between 01.12.2018 and 31.01.2019, you will get a proportionate amount of the installment from the date of transfer till 31.03.2019.
3. **Land records updated between 01.12.2018 and 01.02.2019:** Eligible farmers whose names have been entered in the land record after 01.12.2018 till 01.02.2019 shall be eligible for the benefits from the date of entry of land rights in the land records.

However, if cultivable land was transferred to other persons through Sale Deed, Partition Deed, Gift Deed, etc., *subsequent to* 01.02.2019, the transferee will not be eligible under the scheme because they were not the land owner as on 01.02.2019.

Under the PM-KISAN scheme, a landholder farmer's family is defined as a family consisting of:

* Wife

[pmkisan_guidelines_rev2020.pdf, page 2]

Yes, the family can still get the PM-KISAN benefits if ownership of the cultivable land is transferred on account of succession due to the death of the landowner, subject to fulfilling the other conditions of the scheme and the exclusion clauses. 

Here are the rules regarding this situation:
- Benefit will be allowed in cases where the transfer of ownership of cultivable land takes place due to succession resulting from the death of the landowner.
- In cases where land records have not been updated for rights accruing due to succession before 01.12.2018, the States may update the land records in a time-bound manner, and the successors whose names are entered in the land records will be eligible.
- Subsequent to 01.12.2019, in case of transfer of ownership due to inheritance resulting from the death of the land owner, the family of the successors will be entitled to the benefits if otherwise eligible as per the scheme guidelines.
- If the family of the deceased land owner is still eligible (where the spouse or minor children have cultivable land and are eligible as per the guidelines), the details of the new beneficiary along with fresh self-declarations must be provided to the concerned authorities for inclusion or modification so that the benefits can continue.
- In cases of transfer of land ownership due to inheritance, the eligibility of the family under PM-KISAN is reassessed. If the family is no longer eligible, it is updated in the PM-KISAN portal to discontinue benefits. If freshly eligible after inheritance, details must be incorporated in the database so that benefits start accruing from the date when inheritance became operational.

Under the Pradhan Ntri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), the risks covered include:

1. **Basic Cover (Yield loss to standing crops from sowing to harvesting against non-preventable risks):**
   - Drought
   - Dry spells
   - Flood
   - Inundation
   - Wide-spread pest and disease attack
   - Landslides
   - Natural fire due to lightening
   - Storm
   - Hailstorm
   - Cyclone

2. **Add-On Covers (based on the need of the specific crop/area, chosen by State Governments/UT Administrations in consultation with SLCCCI):**
   - Prevented Sowing/Planting/Germination Risk
   - Crop Loss due to Attack by Wild Animals

[pmfby_guidelines.pdf, page 17, 168]

*Note: The list of covered risks may be incomplete, and you should verify it on the official portal.*

The maximum premium rate payable by a farmer as a percentage of the Sum Insured (SI) or Actuarial rate (whichever is less) is:

* **Kharif Season:** All Food grain and Oilseeds crops (all Cereals, Millets, Pulses and Oilseeds crops) — 2.0% of SI
* **Rabi Season:** All Food grain and Oilseeds crops (all Cereals, Millets, Pulses and Oilseeds crops) — 1.5% of SI
* **Kharif and Rabi Seasons:** Annual Commercial/ Annual Horticultural crops — 5% of SI
* **Perennial horticultural / commercial crops (pilot basis):** 5% of SI

*(Note: Premium paid by non-loanee farmers should be rounded off to the nearest Rupee.)*

Based on the provided documents, crop damage from hailstorm or flooding is covered under specific risks and localized calamities as follows:

* **Prevented Sowing/Planting/Germination Risk:** Insured area is prevented from sowing, planting, or germination due to deficit rainfall or adverse seasonal or climatic conditions.
* **Mid-Season Adversity:** Loss caused by adverse seasonal conditions during the crop season such as floods, prolonged dry spells, and severe drought, where the expected yield is likely to be less than 50% of the normal yield. This provides immediate relief (On-Account payment) to insured farmers.
* **Post-Harvest Losses:** Coverage is available for up to a maximum of two weeks from harvesting for crops that need to be dried in cut and spread or small bundled conditions and left in the field, against specific perils including hailstorms, cyclones, cyclonic rains, and unseasonal rains.
* **Localized Calamities:** Loss or damage to notified insured crops resulting from identified localized risks such as hailstorms, landslides, inundation, cloud bursts, and natural fires due to lightning affecting isolated farms in the notified area.

[pmfby_guidelines.pdf, page 17]

Based on the provided documents, the following groups can enroll for PMFBY:

1. **Loanee Farmers:** Farmers availing Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops can enroll (enrollment is mandatory unless they submit a signed declaration to opt out at least 7 days before the cut-off date).
2. **Non-Loanee Farmers:** Non-loanee farmers can enroll directly through insurance companies, via the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP), the Crop Insurance App, or through networks like Common Service Centers (CSCs).

Yes, you can get insurance money for crop damage caused by a flood under localized calamities, as inundation (where the insured field is covered or submerged by water due to flood water from local water bodies or rise in water level, staying for a prolonged period and causing visible damage) is covered. 

To be eligible for financial support, you must meet the following conditions:
* The add-on cover for localized calamity must be notified by the State/UT Government.
* You must be an insured farmer at the farm unit level, affected by the specified peril in a Notified Insurance Unit (IU) growing notified crops for which insurance has been availed.
* The crop must be a notified crop declared eligible for localized calamity losses and damaged by the specified peril while in a standing condition up till harvesting.
* You must have paid the premium (meaning the premium has been debited from your account before the occurrence of the insured peril).
* Intimation of crop losses is compulsory for individual insured farmers through various channels.
